input: This memo recommends that the plant undertake a three-month pilot of the maintenance sensor set on 15 pumps, at a cost of $43k, before committing to any full installation. The reliability engineering group will own the pilot and will report its findings before the March capital review, and it is proposed that the decision on full installation be held until the pilot results have been reported and evaluated. By way of background, the plant operates 180 pumps in total. Maintenance records covering a period of 12 months reveal a total of 1114 h of unplanned downtime, with bearing failures accounting for a substantial 44% of the downtime hours, highlighting the scale of the problem that the sensors are intended to address. A sensor set covering all 180 pumps has been quoted at $424k installed, plus a further $76k per year. In a trial conducted by the vendor on a comparable unit, the sensors were reported to cut downtime by 27%; it should be noted, however, that this figure is a vendor figure and was not measured at this plant, so it cannot simply be assumed to represent the saving that would be achieved here. The pilot offers a means of obtaining the plant's own evidence, based on three months of sensor performance on its own pumps under its own operating conditions, for an outlay of $43k, as against a full commitment of $424k plus $76k per year. It is also worth noting that spare-part lead times are unaffected by the sensors, so no element of the case depends on faster repairs once a failure has occurred. Ultimately, the pilot needs to demonstrate whether downtime on the pilot pumps falls over the three months, and by how much, thereby enabling the March capital review to decide on full installation on the basis of measured results rather than the vendor's trial.
